measurement_kind: Terminal-log emitted-result interval observations, not standalone module benchmarks.
method: Parse only the declared test command regions and reconcile every recorded ID with the frozen inventory and saved job ledgers.
An observed module span is its first-to-last emitted completion timestamp; it omits setup before the first result and cleanup after the last result.
Entry-to-last-result proxies start at the preceding result or command log timestamp. They may include preceding-module cleanup, loading, setup, and logging delay; they are not exact module runtimes.
Censored observed spans provide lower-bound observations only. Missing results and unobserved modules are not zero-cost tests.
The cancellation tail is unattributed because no uncompleted start record survived; the next static method is not assumed to have started.
Partition sums regroup observations from the original order. Parallel jobs change global order and process isolation; sums are not forecasts or a guarantee of fitting six hours.
Windows selected profiles cover 526 methods only. They are not full-Linux or full-core evidence and are not substituted for missing Ubuntu measurements.

validation.initial_discovery_attempt: System Python lacked jsonschema; discovery failed before a manifest was written. A read-only existing development environment was then used successfully.

conclusion.required_followup: Measure the actual frozen partitions under each supported Ubuntu Python version. Stop for a separate plan if a whole module cannot fit the six-hour ceiling; do not split methods silently.
